title: Where a host is plugged in, its port, the switch's uplink, the other end of it, and its flaps today and yesterday

turns.answer: On `access-sw2.example.net`, port `Gi1/0/5 (desk 5)`, VLAN `10`: its MAC `00:11:22:33:44:55` was last seen there `1h 0m` ago. core-sw1 learned it too, on `Gi1/0/2`, its trunk to access-sw2, so that is not where it is plugged in.

turns.user: What speed is that port running at?
turns.answer: `1G`, `full` duplex, and it is `up`, carrying `10 Mbit/s` out and `1.2 Mbit/s` in, with no open alerts.
`Gi1/0/48 (to core-sw1)`, to `core-sw1.example.net` port `Gi1/0/2`: both ends `1G`, full duplex, MTU `1500`, no mismatches.
`Gi1/0/2` on core-sw1 is `up`, with no errors and no open alerts, but it last changed state only `29m 0s` ago.

turns.user: Has that link been flapping today?
turns.answer: Once: it went down and came back up, the last change at `2026-10-28T11:31:00Z` (`ifOperStatus: down -> up`).

Yesterday evening too: down at `2026-10-27T18:00:00Z`, back up at `2026-10-27T18:05:00Z`. With today's drop at `2026-10-28T11:30:00Z`, that is twice in a day. LibreNMS does not say why; the switches' syslog may.
